```plato
    // The buoyant force on a body displacing `submerged` of fluid, given the local
    // gravitational acceleration: minus the weight of the displaced fluid, by
    // Archimedes' principle. The caller computes the submerged volume, because
    // that is a query against the body's shape and the fluid half-space.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archimedes%27_principle)
    BuoyantForce(self: BuoyancyModel, submerged: Volume, gravity: Vector3D): Vector3D
        => gravity.Negative * (self.FluidDensity.Amount * submerged.Amount);

    //==
    // # Mass properties and inertia tensors
    //
    // The inertia of the primitive solids, about the CENTRE OF MASS and in the
    // shape's own PRINCIPAL frame, where the tensor is diagonal and three numbers
    // say everything. `PrincipalMoments` returns those three; `InertiaTensor`
    // packs them into the `SymmetricMatrix3x3` that `MassProperties3D` declares.
    //
    // Every formula is for a solid of UNIFORM DENSITY, and every one takes the
    // mass rather than a density, because mass is the quantity a caller usually
    // knows and `MassOf` derives it from a density when it does not.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_moments_of_inertia)

    // A diagonal inertia tensor from the three principal moments, in
    // kilogram-square-meters.
    DiagonalInertia(moments: Vector3D): SymmetricMatrix3x3
        => SymmetricMatrix3x3(moments.X, 0.0, 0.0, moments.Y, 0.0, moments.Z);

    // The principal moments a diagonal tensor was built from. Reading only the
    // diagonal is exact when the tensor IS diagonal — which is the case for every
    // shape in this section — and is the principal-frame approximation otherwise.
    PrincipalMoments(tensor: SymmetricMatrix3x3): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(tensor.M11, tensor.M22, tensor.M33);

    // The inertia tensor of the same body about an axis system displaced by
    // `offset` from the centre of mass: the parallel-axis (Huygens-Steiner)
    // theorem, I' = I + m (|d|^2 E - d d^T). Note that the shifted tensor has
    // off-diagonal terms even when the original does not — a displaced body is not
    // principal about the displaced axes, which is exactly why a compound body
    // needs the full tensor and a primitive does not.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_axis_theorem)
    ShiftedInertia(tensor: SymmetricMatrix3x3, mass: Mass, offset: Vector3D): SymmetricMatrix3x3
    {
        var m = mass.Amount;
        var d2 = offset.MagnitudeSquared;
        return SymmetricMatrix3x3(
            tensor.M11 + m * (d2 - offset.X * offset.X),
            tensor.M12 - m * offset.X * offset.Y,
            tensor.M13 - m * offset.X * offset.Z,
            tensor.M22 + m * (d2 - offset.Y * offset.Y),
            tensor.M23 - m * offset.Y * offset.Z,
            tensor.M33 + m * (d2 - offset.Z * offset.Z));
    }

    // The sum of two inertia tensors, which is how a compound body's tensor is
    // built: shift each part to the common centre of mass, then add.
    CombinedInertia(a: SymmetricMatrix3x3, b: SymmetricMatrix3x3): SymmetricMatrix3x3
        => SymmetricMatrix3x3(
            a.M11 + b.M11, a.M12 + b.M12, a.M13 + b.M13,
            a.M22 + b.M22, a.M23 + b.M23, a.M33 + b.M33);

    // The moment of inertia about a unit axis through the centre of mass:
    // axis^T I axis. Precondition: `axis` is unit, which `Direction3D` promises.
    InertiaAbout(tensor: SymmetricMatrix3x3, axis: Direction3D): MomentOfInertia
    {
        var d = axis.Vector;
        return MomentOfInertia.FromAmount(
            tensor.M11 * d.X * d.X + tensor.M22 * d.Y * d.Y + tensor.M33 * d.Z * d.Z
            + 2.0 * (tensor.M12 * d.X * d.Y + tensor.M13 * d.X * d.Z + tensor.M23 * d.Y * d.Z));
    }

    // The mass of a solid of the given volume at the given uniform density.
    MassOf(volume: Volume, density: Density): Mass
        => Mass.FromAmount(volume.Amount * density.Amount);

    // The principal moments of a solid ball: 2/5 m r^2 about every axis through
    // the centre — a ball has no distinguished axis, so its tensor is a multiple
    // of the identity and stays diagonal under any rotation.
    PrincipalMoments(s: Sphere, mass: Mass): Vector3D
    {
        var i = 0.4 * mass.Amount * s.Radius.Square;
        return Vector3D(i, i, i);
    }

    // The principal moments of a solid box about its own axes: m (b^2 + c^2) / 12
    // per axis, over the two FULL extents perpendicular to it.
    PrincipalMoments(b: Box3D, mass: Mass): Vector3D
    {
        var k = mass.Amount / 12.0;
        var w = b.Size.Width.Square;
        var h = b.Size.Height.Square;
        var d = b.Size.Depth.Square;
        return Vector3D(k * (h + d), k * (w + d), k * (w + h));
    }

    // The principal moments of a solid right circular cylinder, in a frame whose
    // LOCAL Z runs along the cylinder's axis: m r^2 / 2 about the axis and
    // m (3 r^2 + h^2) / 12 across it, over the FULL height.
    PrincipalMoments(c: Cylinder, mass: Mass): Vector3D
    {
        var m = mass.Amount;
        var across = m * (3.0 * c.Radius.Square + c.Height.Square) / 12.0;
        return Vector3D(across, across, 0.5 * m * c.Radius.Square);
    }

    // The principal moments of a solid capsule, in a frame whose LOCAL Z runs from
    // A to B: a cylinder of the spine's length capped by two hemispheres, each
    // contributing its own inertia plus a parallel-axis shift to the capsule's
    // centre. The two masses are split by volume, so the result depends on the
    // radius and the spine length only through the ratio of the two parts.
    PrincipalMoments(c: Capsule3D, mass: Mass): Vector3D
    {
        var r = c.Radius;
        var h = c.A.Distance(c.B);
        var cylinderVolume = Number.Pi * r.Square * h;
        var capVolume = 2.0 / 3.0 * Number.Pi * r.Square * r;
        var total = cylinderVolume + 2.0 * capVolume;
        var mc = total > 0.0 ? mass.Amount * cylinderVolume / total : 0.0;
        var mh = total > 0.0 ? mass.Amount * capVolume / total : 0.0;
        var along = 0.5 * mc * r.Square + 2.0 * mh * 0.4 * r.Square;
        var across = mc * (h.Square / 12.0 + r.Square * 0.25)
            + 2.0 * mh * (0.4 * r.Square + h.Square * 0.25 + 0.375 * h * r);
        return Vector3D(across, across, along);
    }

    // The mass properties of a solid ball of uniform density, in a body frame
    // centred on the ball: the centre of mass is the origin of that frame.
    MassPropertiesOf(s: Sphere, density: Density): MassProperties3D
    {
        var mass = MassOf(Volume.FromAmount(s.Volume), density);
        return MassProperties3D(mass, Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), DiagonalInertia(PrincipalMoments(s, mass)));
    }

    // The mass properties of a solid box of uniform density, in the box's own
    // frame.
    MassPropertiesOf(b: Box3D, density: Density): MassProperties3D
    {
        var mass = MassOf(Volume.FromAmount(b.Volume), density);
        return MassProperties3D(mass, Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), DiagonalInertia(PrincipalMoments(b, mass)));
    }

    // The mass properties of a solid cylinder of uniform density, in a frame whose
    // local Z runs along the cylinder's axis.
    MassPropertiesOf(c: Cylinder, density: Density): MassProperties3D
    {
        var mass = MassOf(Volume.FromAmount(c.Volume), density);
        return MassProperties3D(mass, Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), DiagonalInertia(PrincipalMoments(c, mass)));
    }

    // The mass properties of a solid capsule of uniform density, in a frame whose
    // local Z runs from A to B.
    MassPropertiesOf(c: Capsule3D, density: Density): MassProperties3D
    {
        var mass = MassOf(Volume.FromAmount(c.Volume), density);
        return MassProperties3D(mass, Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), DiagonalInertia(PrincipalMoments(c, mass)));
    }
```
